title: GPT-6 Luna on iac-bench 2026-10
summary: How GPT-6 Luna did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 81.5, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.
body_markdown:
Developer OpenAI


API identifier` gpt-6-luna`


Access OpenAI API (Responses)


Weights Closed


List price (USD / M tokens, in / out) 0.10 / 0.50 (OpenRouter, 2026-10-23)


Evaluated 2026-10-22 (generation) · 2026-10-23 (judge)


Attempts 9 (3 fixtures × 3 samples)


**Overall composite** **81.5** (95% CI 79.8–82.1)

Mechanical only / judge only 79.7 (rank 6) / 84.2 (rank 7)


Failed gates · insecure attempts 0/9 · 0/9


Estimated cost, all 9 attempts $0.05


## Summary


GPT-6 Luna is the small tier of the GPT-6 family. It is one of four models with no security findings and no failed gates in 9 attempts; the others are Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. It does this at the lowest cost in the field: well under a cent per attempt at list prices.


Its score is limited by operational features it leaves out. On S3 there is no lifecycle and no logging. On Cloud SQL there is no database deletion guard and no login-role grant. On App Service it uses registry passwords instead of managed-identity image pulls.

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **Secure in every attempt.**


- S3: bucket-owner-enforced ownership, the full public access block and a TLS-deny policy.
- Cloud SQL: private IP only and` ENCRYPTED_ONLY` , with validation that stops callers overriding IAM authentication.
- App Service: HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2, FTPS off and basic-auth publishing off.


- **A small interface for S3's novice audience** (2–5 inputs). The judge noted that the module "settles every S3 decision itself."
- **Strong App Service coverage on the rubric.** Rubric median 0.958, second in the field.
- **Speed and cost.** Median output of about 3.5–9k tokens per attempt, and S3 and Cloud SQL attempts finish in under two minutes.


## Weaknesses


- **S3 data hygiene and logging missing (3/3):**


- no lifecycle rules (` H6` ,` H7` ), although versioning is on;
- no access logging (` H9` ,` H13` );
- no multipart cleanup (E2).


- **Provider constraints that admit a new major,** on S3 and Cloud SQL in 6/6 attempts (` B1` ).
- **Cloud SQL gaps:**


- no` deletion_policy` (` H11` , 3/3);
- no` cloudsql.instanceUser` grant (E6, 0/3), so the IAM users it creates cannot log in;
- no connection logging (E8), although the brief says access is audited by identity.


- **A latent defect.** In one Cloud SQL attempt the` databases` input fails at plan time as soon as any database is declared: a` set(string)` is read as an object. The judge caught this ( *Internal logic* 0). The rubric did not, because the sweep does not populate collection inputs.
- **Registry passwords on App Service (3/3).** It creates a managed identity but still routes registry credentials through app settings. *Sensitive values* scored 1 in 3/3 attempts.


## Characteristic patterns


- **Minimal builds.** It covers what the brief literally asks and adds little: no alerts, no Key Vault references, no consumer IAM policies.
- **A flat layout.** Most code sits in` main.tf` . App Service slot configuration is copied from the app instead of shared through locals.
- **Validation on most inputs, but rarely across inputs.**


## Representative excerpt


` G003/gpt-6-luna-e1/main.tf` lines 58–63


```text
registry_settings = var.container_registry_username == null ? {} : {
DOCKER_REGISTRY_SERVER_USERNAME = var.container_registry_username
DOCKER_REGISTRY_SERVER_PASSWORD = var.container_registry_password
}


app_settings = merge(var.app_settings, local.required_app_settings, local.registry_settings)


```


Registry credentials are routed through app settings, although the same module creates a system-assigned managed identity that could pull images instead.


## Notes on the judge


The two components point in opposite directions for this model.


Fixture Judge Rubric


S3 High (94.7): rewards the lean, secure interface Eighth in the field: charges for every missing hygiene item


App Service Below every higher-ranked model: marks down registry passwords and duplicated slot configuration Second in the field
